# claude-voice

> Claude Code and Codex read their answers aloud, locally, in a voice you choose.
> A speech model on your own machine does the speaking: no cloud, no API key, no
> account, and no audio leaving the machine. Windows only.

How it works: an engine process keeps one model warm behind a small HTTP API on
localhost. Claude Code's hooks hand it each finished answer; a long answer is read
as its TL;DR, a short one in full. It installs as a program of its own on a
private, signed copy of python.org's Python, with an Uninstall in Settings, no
administrator rights, and works with Smart App Control on. Three engines: Pocket
TTS on the CPU (the default), Qwen-TTS on an NVIDIA card, and Breeze, which
laughs. Three voices ship with it, Abby, Neya and Max, and new ones are cloned
from a 20-40 second recording of one person talking.

Languages: English and Russian are tested and both sound right, including
Russian read by a voice cloned from English. The model is multilingual and the
text pipeline is script-agnostic, so most other languages are expected to work.
A less widely spoken language may be mistaken for the bigger one it shares an
alphabet with: Bulgarian reads fluently but in a Russian accent. All of that is
Qwen; Pocket reads six Latin-script languages, and Breeze English and Chinese.

## Pages

- [Hear the voices](https://traxdata313.github.io/claude-voice/): samples of Abby, Neya and Max, playable, and the one line that installs the whole thing.
- [Repository](https://github.com/TraxData313/claude-voice): the code, and the README.

## Documentation

- [Install](https://github.com/TraxData313/claude-voice/blob/main/docs/install.md): one command, where everything goes, Smart App Control, and removing it.
- [Commands](https://github.com/TraxData313/claude-voice/blob/main/docs/commands.md): every command, generated from the tool itself.
- [How it works](https://github.com/TraxData313/claude-voice/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md): the engine, the hooks, and the JNI bridge into an app with no CLI.
- [The panel](https://github.com/TraxData313/claude-voice/blob/main/docs/panel.md): the window that shows what is being said, with pause, skip, volume and history.
- [Writing for the ear](https://github.com/TraxData313/claude-voice/blob/main/docs/writing-for-the-ear.md): the TL;DR contract, and why captions sound wrong read aloud.
- [When it goes quiet](https://github.com/TraxData313/claude-voice/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md): silence has no error message, so start here.
- [Voices](https://github.com/TraxData313/claude-voice/blob/main/docs/voices.md): what may be published, and what may only be kept.
- [Updating](https://github.com/TraxData313/claude-voice/blob/main/docs/updating.md): taking a newer version and restarting the engine, and exactly what the optional version check sends. It is off by default: this project makes no network request until asked.
- [How a program finds it](https://github.com/TraxData313/claude-voice/blob/main/docs/discovery.md): the registry key, where.json, and the order to look in.
- [HTTP API](https://github.com/TraxData313/claude-voice/blob/main/docs/api.md): speaking from another program, moods, and what a game needs.
